# Jānis Ruško (Janis Rusko)

Jānis Ruško, professionally also using the name Janis Rusko, is a senior expert in chemical risk assessment at BIOR in Riga. His work focuses on chemical risk assessment for food safety, integrated chemical evidence, dietary exposure assessment, risk-benefit assessment, risk prioritisation, evidence synthesis, guidance, and policy-facing decision support.

Analytical chemistry and non-target analysis are the technical foundation of the profile. The current research direction is evidence infrastructure for chemical risk assessment: structuring fragmented evidence, improving prioritisation, and developing practical decision-support methods.

## Current Emphasis

- Integrated evidence infrastructure combining monitoring and occurrence data, food-consumption information, toxicological reference values, scientific literature, and predictive toxicology evidence. AI-assisted literature extraction is one supporting method for expanding and structuring occurrence evidence.
- Transparent risk-ranking, uncertainty, and monitoring-prioritisation methods for identifying evidence gaps and directing assessment and monitoring resources.
- Applied exposure, chemical-risk, and risk-benefit assessments designed for interpretable conclusions, proportionate guidance, and policy-facing decisions.

## Selected Work

- From Data to Decisions: principal investigator, postdoctoral research project 1.1.1.9/LZP/1/24/124, 2025–2028. Building a harmonised chemical-contaminant occurrence database for Latvian food and feed. The combined contaminants taxonomy and database specification are completed; ongoing work links occurrence evidence with toxicological reference values and food-consumption data to develop risk-prioritisation methods. Official project page: https://bior.lv/en/projekts/the-scientific-institute-bior-in-cooperation-with-the-latvian-council-of-science-lcs-is-implementing-the-research-application-no-1-1-1-9-lzp-1-24-124-from-data-to-decis/
- Contaminants in edible bee products: coordinates literature search, screening and data extraction within BeSafeBeeHoney Working Group 2, covering honey, pollen, bee bread, royal jelly and propolis. https://www.cost.eu/actions/CA22105/
- Drinking-water risk assessment and monitoring: led the 2023–2026 development, validation and delivery of BIOR's national toolkit to Latvia's Ministry of Health, covering more than 200 parameters.
- Fish consumption: compiled contaminant and nutritional-composition evidence for SEAwise and led BIOR's GreenAgroRes task, including survey design and fish-sampling coordination. First author of the 2026 Latvian inland-fish pilot risk-benefit assessment.

## Selected Outputs

- 2026: Glyphosate in apiculture: occurrence patterns across honey, pollen, and beebread. Food Control. Co-author; occurrence evidence. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.foodcont.2025.111649

- 2026: Deterministic Pilot Risk-Benefit Assessment of Latvian Inland Fish: Safe Weekly Consumption Guidance. Foods. Risk-benefit guidance. https://doi.org/10.3390/foods15050901
- 2021: Phenolic Profiles of Raw Mono- and Polyfloral Honeys from Latvia. Journal of Food Composition and Analysis. Analytical foundation. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfca.2021.103813
- 2020: Non-target and Suspected-target Screening for Potentially Hazardous Chemicals in Food Contact Materials: Investigation of Paper Straws. Food Additives & Contaminants: Part A. Non-target screening. https://doi.org/10.1080/19440049.2020.1711969
- 2021: Rapid Determination of Pharmaceuticals in Wastewater by Direct Infusion HRMS Using Target and Suspect Screening Analysis. Science of the Total Environment. Screening methods. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.scitotenv.2020.142688

## Credentials

- Senior expert in chemical risk assessment at BIOR.
- Alternate member of EFSA's Management Board, 2022-present.
- PhD in Chemistry, University of Latvia (2021), focused on non-target screening and high-resolution mass spectrometry.
- COST Management Committee member for Latvia: Agrifood-OneAI (CA25159; starts September 2026) and BeSafeBeeHoney (CA22105).

## Teaching and Professional Training

- Teaches food-safety and chemical-risk assessment at Rīga Stradiņš University, the University of Latvia and Riga Technical University. Experience includes BSc/MSc thesis supervision and co-supervision in analytical chemistry and food authenticity.
- Contracted BTSF tutor, 2024–2025: modules on veterinary medicinal product authorisation, risk-based residue surveillance and import controls, delivered in Puławy, Dublin and Brescia to laboratory staff from non-EU countries.
- EFSA EU-FORA fellow, CNR Institute of Protein Biochemistry, Naples, 2017–2018: co-developed automated enzymatic biosensors for pesticide-contamination assessment.
